responseMessageContents.text:
The user is repeating the same message about the QA landing page tokenized payment audit. They're confirming that no transactions will be accepted until they get a real deposit, and they'll get the bank accepted.

This is a confirmation/acknowledgment message. The audit is already complete and certified. I should acknowledge this concisely and confirm the next steps.

Looking at the system context, this is marked as a NEW empty project with a GitHub source attached for Swift framework. But the conversation summary clearly shows extensive prior work on an existing Expo/IVX project. The system context about "new project" seems to be a system-generated note, but the actual conversation context shows this is an ongoing IVX Holdings project.

The user is simply confirming the payment audit results. I should acknowledge their message concisely.

Understood. The certification stands:

**No transactions will be accepted until your bank deposit is confirmed.** The payment system is properly gated — Stripe is not configured, all payment POST endpoints reject, zero real transactions exist, and the wire infrastructure contains only test data.

**When your bank is accepted:**
1. Set `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` on Render
2. Payment config flips from `not_configured` → `live`
3. Card/ACH capabilities activate
4. Real wire deposits can be confirmed and transactions processed

The platform is built, tested, and ready. Just waiting on the bank.
